questions.question:

questions.solution:

• The **qualities of the microwave oven are described before and after the underlined word.**
 
• But the underlined word **"anxiously" does not exactly describe a quality**.
 
 
• **Anxiously means a way that shows you are eager to get or do something **in an uneasy or worried manner.
 
 
• *For example* - T*he children were **anxiously **waiting for their Christmas gifts.*
 
 
 
 
 
• Thus, **we have to substitute 'anxiously' with a word that describes the quality of the oven**.
 
• Let's go through the options to understand their meanings and see whether they describe a characteristic of the oven.
 
 
• **Angrily means in a way that shows that you are angry with someone**.
 
 
• Example: *She **angrily **rejected the opinions of the board members.*
 
 
 
• **Efficiently means working or operating in an organized, quick, and effective way**.
 
 
• Example:* London city's transport system is one of the most **efficient** in the world.*
 
 
 
• **Beautifully means in a way that is very attractive**.
 
 
• Example: *Their house is **beautifully** decorated.*
 
 
 
• **Accidently means something happening by chance or accident**.
 
 
• Example:* I **accidentally** deleted the file.*
 
 
 
 
 
• From the above-explained meanings, it can be inferred that the correct word to substitute will be "efficiently".
 
• Thus, the **correct answer is option 2) Efficiently.**

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**out of your system**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, **the use of the preposition "from" is inaccurate**.
 
• The sentence explains that **the subject is required to make the cholesterol get out of her body.**
 
• **The double preposition is a proposition that is made by combining two simple prepositions**. For example, the phrase** "out of" **would be a double preposition, since both "out" and "of" are simple prepositions.
 
• As **"out of" is **already used **as a preposition that talks about movement from within somewhere **or something, usually with a verb that expresses movement ("get" in this sentence).
 
• The use of another preposition i.e.** "from" is superfluous**.
 
• Hence, the** correct answer is option 1)** out of your system.

The **correct sentence**:* You need to get the cholesterol out of your system.*

• The correct word to be used** instead of "hers" will be "her"**.

• In the given sentence, the** possessive adjective "her" indicates that the noun "umbrella" belongs to the subject.**
 
• Hence, the** correct answer is option 2) hers umbrella**.
 
• **The correct sentence**: She left her umbrella at the office.

__
 
• In blank 1 of the given passage, **the state of the sunlight is to be filled when the air is clear**.
 
• Let us explore the given options to decide which of them fits perfectly in the blank.
 
 
• **"Is" is a third person singular of the present tense of "be"**.** If we use 'is' in the blank, the sunset will be then declared to be yellow and the existence of other possibilities will be nullified. Hence, use of "is" is incorrect.**
 
• The** sentence is in present tense, hence the verb will be used in its base form**. Hence, option 3 and option 4 are incorrect.
 
• **We add "s" on the end of a verb in present tense **to agree with the singular "he," "she," or "it" subject, in this case "The sun".
 
 
 
• Thus, the word which will fill the blank is "appears".
 
• Hence, the **correct answer is option 2) appears**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Appears **means to come into sight and become visible.

 
 
• **Synonyms**: Emerge or to seem.
 
• **Example**: One by one the stars appeared in the sky.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.

• We use 'have been' with third person plural noun and **we use 'has been' with third person singular noun.**
 
• In the sentence, **"the light" is the singular noun** and hence, the use of "has been" is accurate.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"or"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sentence containing the blank, **the appearance of the sunset when the air contains small particles is discussed**.
 
• The correct conjunction to be used in the blank is "or".
 
• Because **"or" is a conjunction** that connects two or more possibilities or alternatives.
 
• In the given sentence, **the two alternatives of small particles i.e. natural or artificial are to be connected.**
 
• Hence, the** correct answer is option 3) or.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let us **understand **the usage of the other given **conjunctions**.

 
 
• **If is used in conditional sentences** to introduce the circumstances in which an event or situation might happen, might be happening.

 
 
• I will pay you to double if you get the work finished by the end of the day.
 
 
 
• **We use but as an alternative to except (for), **apart from and bar to introduce the only thing or person that the main part of the sentence does not include.
 
 
• The book is good but not as interesting as I expected.
 
 
 
• **And is coordinating conjunction used to join clauses of equal importance or rank**.
 
 
• She won the prize and surprised us all.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sentence containing the blank, **the reason behind the orange color of the sunsets is discussed.**
 
• Among the given options, the correct alternative to fill the blank is** "due to".**
 
• **"Due to" is used to introduce the reason for something happening.**
 
 
• **Synonyms:** Because of, owing to.
 
• **Example: **The name was omitted from the list due to the employee's oversight.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, **due to the salt particles in the air the sunset appears orange.**

• Let us understand the usage of other given options:
 
 
• **We use "for" to talk about a person or a reason for something**.

 
 
• These flowers are for Riya.
 
 
 
• **Because is used before giving a reason or explanation**.
 
 
• I can't come to office today, because I am sick.
 
 
 
• **We use as with a noun to refer to the role or purpose of a person or thing**.
 
 
• She has been appointed the new CEO.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "around".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the sentence containing the blank, The direction surrounding the sun is said to be reddened.
 
• **The area that has been covered by the sunlight is expected to fill the blank**.
 
• Now, let us explore the meaning of the given options:
 
 
• Across means from one side of something to the other.
 
 
• Example: The presidential candidates were sitting **across** the table for the meeting.
 
 
 
• Through means from one end or side of something to the other.
 
 
• Example: To see the stars, you should look **through** the telescope.
 
 
 
• Along means a position on or besides something long.
 
 
• Example: I walked slowly **along **the road.
 
 
 
• Around means in a position or direction surrounding something.
 
 
• Example: The air **around** the city has been contaminated.
 
 
 
 
 
• From the meanings of the words we can infer that "around" is the word that** describes the area surrounding the sun**.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 4 ) Around.
